meta.title: ProxMenux Monitor — Dashboard: System Logs tab | ProxMenux Documentation
meta.description: The System Logs tab consolidates three sources into one screen: live journalctl with filters and download, Proxmox task history (UPIDs), and notification log — all searchable, filterable by severity / time range, and downloadable as text bundles.

header.title: Dashboard: System Logs tab
header.description: Three sub-tabs under one roof: the system journal (journalctl with filters), Proxmox task history, and the notification log. All three are searchable, filterable and downloadable as text bundles.

readOnly.title: Read-only by design
readOnly.body: Nothing on this tab modifies log files. Filters live in the URL / state, downloads are server-side bundles. The dashboard never deletes log entries — for housekeeping use the host's own journalctl --vacuum-time=<N> or logrotate.

topRow.heading: Top row: four counters
items: Total Entries — number of log records inside the active filter window.
Backups: number of backup archives on the configured backup storages.

subtabs.heading: Three sub-tabs
subtabs.logsIntro: The system journal, served by journalctl on the backend. Filters available in the toolbar:
logsFilters: Level: All levels, Error, Warning or Info.
Time range: 1 day / 3 days / 1 week / 2 weeks / 1 month, or a custom number of days (up to 90).
Free-text search: case-insensitive substring over message, service, PID, hostname and unit, applied in the browser.
Service filter: restrict to one service (the journal SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER).
subtabs.logsRowsAfter: Each row shows timestamp, severity badge, source unit and the message. Long messages collapse with a "show more" toggle. The Download action bundles the current filter into a single .txt file via GET /api/logs/download — useful when you want to share a slice of journal with someone.
subtabs.logDetailsBody: Clicking any row opens a Log Details modal with every structured field journald captured for that single entry — the same view you'd build by hand running journalctl --output=verbose on the host.
subtabs.logDetailsImageAlt: Log Details modal — single journal entry expanded with Level, Service, Timestamp, Source, Systemd Unit, Process ID, Hostname and the full Message
subtabs.logDetailsImageCaption: Log Details modal — every structured field journald carries for this entry, with the full untruncated message at the bottom. Useful for cron and service logs where the executed command line matters.
fields: Level — coloured severity badge (INFO / WARNING / ERROR / CRITICAL).
Service — short name of the unit / process that emitted the entry.
Timestamp — full date and time of the log line.
Source — origin of the entry (journal, kernel, audit, …).
Systemd Unit — the actual .service / .timer / .socket unit if the entry was associated with one.
Process ID — PID of the emitting process.
Hostname — useful when journals are forwarded across cluster nodes.
Message — the full untruncated message in a monospace block, ready to copy.
subtabs.maxLevelStoreBody: On a fresh Proxmox install, journald defaults to MaxLevelStore=warning, which silently drops info-level messages. The Monitor detects this on startup and adds a drop-in (/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/proxmenux-loglevel.conf) raising the threshold to info so informational and more severe messages are stored. This does not include debug messages.
subtabs.backupsBody: The backup archives on every backup-capable storage (dir, NFS, CIFS, PBS), read with pvesh get /nodes/localhost/storage/<id>/content. Cards at the top show the VM and LXC counts and the total size; below, one row per archive with type, storage, size and date. Restore lives in the Proxmox web UI.
subtabs.notificationsBody1: Proxmox notification activity: journal lines from Proxmox services that mention notifications, email, webhooks or alerts, the targets in /etc/pve/notifications.cfg, and backup tasks from the cluster task list. Backup task rows can download the full task log. The history of what the Monitor itself dispatched lives in Settings → Notifications → Notification history.
subtabs.notificationsBody2: Use this tab to check what Proxmox's own notification system is doing. Monitor channel configuration lives in the <link>Notifications</link> deep page.

dataCollected.heading: How the data is collected

rows.source: The tab requests /api/logs?since_days=N; level, service and text filters run in the browser. The API also accepts priority and service, which the tab does not use yet.
Same query, returned as plain text for grep / less.
Backup archives listed from each backup storage with pvesh get /nodes/localhost/storage/<id>/content.
Plain-text full task log read from /var/log/pve/tasks/<index>/<upid>.
journalctl --grep over Proxmox units, /etc/pve/notifications.cfg and backup tasks from pvesh get /cluster/tasks.
